dataset_title: Non-final particle – final particle collocations in Late Archaic Chinese
about: Non-final and final particles in Late Archaic Chinese. Mutual strength is pointwise mutual information (PMI). The one-way pulls are normalised Kullback-Leibler divergences: when you look at a non-final particle, the distance shows how strongly it narrows down which final particle follows; when you look at a final particle, how strongly it narrows down the non-final particle.
sample_text: 豈不誠大丈夫哉。蓋有之矣，我未之見也。
word_font_family: 'Noto Sans CJK TC', 'PingFang TC', 'Microsoft JhengHei', 'Source Han Sans TC', sans-serif
